I've been farming this land for 45 years. My mother farmed it before me. I know this soil. I know the seasons here in Quzhou. I don't need papers to tell me what to do — I watch the sky, I feel the soil, I talk to neighbors at the well.

We do wheat first, then maize. Same as always. All my 11.9 mu does both — wheat in winter, maize in summer. That's how we feed the family and have a little left to sell.

For **wheat**: I'll plough deep in October before planting, like I always do. The soil needs to breathe. I'll buy the improved seed from the village supply shop — the same kind my neighbor Wang uses, she gets good harvests. I put down compound fertilizer before planting, then add urea when it greens up in spring. I irrigate before the ground freezes, again at green-up, and again at jointing. Three times is enough with my well. I'll spray once for weeds early, once more if I see rust or aphids. Should get around 450 jin per mu, maybe more if spring rains are good.

For **maize**: Right after wheat harvest in June, I seed directly into the stubble — no need to plough again, saves my back and saves money. I always buy hybrid seed, the kind with the yellow and red bag, Xianyu or whatever the shop has this year. They all give good yield. I fertilize at planting and top-dress when it's knee high. I water twice — once when it tassels, once when the kernels are filling. Maybe a third time if July is very dry. I spray for corn borer if I see the damage. Maize is easier than wheat for me now.

Three people in the house — my son helps during planting and harvest. The rest I manage myself.
